# Volume 4 — CHAPTER 19 DAWN AND DUSK

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

At the start of June, during a time when the sand hills displayed a grand splendor of pink wild roses and apple blossoms enveloped the Glen, Thirza came to the little house along with a black horsehair trunk decorated with brass nails, a chest that had rested untouched in the Grey Shutters garret for fifty years. Tabitha Pratt had spent her few weeks' stay at the little house growing to adore “young Mrs. Doctor,” her name for Nell, with an unreasoning devotion, causing her to view Thirza with a somewhat envious suspicion initially. However, because Thirza refrained from meddling with affairs in the kitchen and displayed no wish to hinder Tabitha's care of young Mrs. Doctor, the loyal servant made peace with her being there, informing her friends in the Glen that Miss Abernethy was a splendid old woman who understood her place.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0000 }

One night, while the clear vessel of the sky held a crimson brilliance, and the robins were serenading the gilded dusk with joyful songs for the evening stars, an abrupt disturbance occurred in the little house of dreams. Phone calls went out to the Glen, Doctor Dave along with a nurse wearing a white cap arrived in a hurry, Thirza walked back and forth along the garden paths lined with quahog shells, whispering prayers through her clenched lips, and Tabitha remained in the kitchen, her ears stuffed with cotton wool and her apron pulled over her head.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0001 }

Lorna, who observed the small dwelling up the stream from inside the house, noticed that each of its windows was illuminated, which kept her awake throughout the night.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0002 }

The night in June was brief, yet to the ones waiting and watching, it felt like forever.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0003 }

“Oh, will it NEVER end?” Thirza asked; after that, observing the somber expressions of the nurse and Doctor Dave, she did not venture to ask any further questions. Imagine if Nell—yet Thirza was unable to imagine such a thing.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0004 }

“Never say,” declared Tabitha with ferocity, responding to the torment visible in Thirza’s eyes, “that God would act with such cruelty as to rob us of that sweet lamb when each of us holds her so dear.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0005 }

“He has taken other ones who were loved just as much,” Thirza said in a raspy voice.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0006 }

However, as day broke, the ascending sun tore asunder the fog suspended above the shoal and converted it into rainbows, bringing happiness to the small dwelling. Nell had survived, and a tiny, pale female babe, possessing the large eyes of her mother, reposed next to her. Hugh, whose visage appeared ashen and drawn on account of the night’s suffering, descended to inform Thirza and Tabitha.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0007 }

“Thank God,” Thirza shuddered.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0008 }

Rising to her feet, Tabitha removed the cotton wool from her ears.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0009 }

“Time for breakfast now,” she stated in a brisk manner. “It is my belief that some food and drink will be welcomed by us all. Instruct young Mrs. Doctor to be entirely free of concern—Tabitha is taking charge. Instruct her to occupy her thoughts solely with her infant.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0010 }

Hugh offered a somewhat melancholic smile as he departed. Nell, whose pallid countenance was drained by its initiation into suffering, and whose eyes shone with the sacred fervor of maternity, required no prompting to consider her infant. No other thought occupied her mind. Over the course of several hours, she experienced a delight of such unique and refined quality that she pondered whether the heavenly angels might be jealous of her.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0011 }

“Little Joyce,” she whispered, as Thirza entered to look at the infant. “If she turned out to be a girl, that was the name we intended to give her. There were numerous people after whom we wished to name her; because choosing among them was impossible, we settled on Joyce—shortened, we can refer to her as Joy—Joy—it is so fitting. Oh, Thirza, I believed my previous state was happiness. I realize now that I merely experienced a delightful dream of being happy. THIS is real.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0012 }

“Nell, you must not speak—hold off until your strength returns,” Thirza said in a warning tone.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0013 }

“You are aware of how difficult I find it NOT to speak,” Nell smiled.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0014 }

Initially she was too feeble and too joyous to perceive that Hugh and the nurse appeared solemn and Thirza appeared grief-stricken. Afterward, as imperceptibly, and chillily, and pitilessly as a sea-fog drifting toward the shore, dread slithered into her heart. For what reason was Hugh not more joyful? For what reason refused he to speak regarding the infant? For what reason refused they to allow her to keep it beside her following that initial divine—joyous hour? Was—was anything amiss?
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0015 }

“Hugh,” Nell entreated in a whisper, “is the baby—doing fine—or not? Speak to me—speak to me.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0016 }

Hugh took a great deal of time to turn around; after that, he leaned over Nell and peered into her eyes. Outside the door, listening in terror, Thirza caught a sorrowful, despairing groan, and she ran away to the kitchen where Tabitha was crying.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0017 }

“Oh, that unfortunate dear—that unfortunate dear! How is it possible for her to endure this, Miss Abernethy? It will be her death, I fear. That baby was all she anticipated and prepared for, bringing her such joy and hope. Is there really no way to help at all, Miss Abernethy?”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0018 }

“I regret that is not the case, Tabitha. Hugh states that all hope is gone. From the very beginning, he was aware the small creature could not survive.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0019 }

“And that child is so adorable,” wept Tabitha. “Never before have I beheld a newborn so pale—normally they are reddish or yellowish. Furthermore, its large eyes unclosed just like a baby several months along. That tiny, tiny creature! Oh, that tragic, youthful Mrs. Doctor!”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0020 }

When the sun went down, the tiny spirit that had arrived at dawn departed, causing deep grief. Miss Winifred received the small, pale girl from the nurse’s well-meaning yet unfamiliar hands, and she clothed the minuscule, waxy body in the lovely gown Lorna had crafted for the baby. Lorna had requested that she perform this task. Afterwards, she carried the child back and placed it next to the pathetic, crushed, weeping mother.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0021 }

“The Lord gave and the Lord took back, dearie,” weeping herself, she said. “Blessed be the Lord’s name.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0022 }

Afterward she departed, leaving Nell and Hugh by themselves alongside their deceased.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0023 }

On the following day, a velvet casket, lined with apple-blossoms by Lorna, received the small white Joy, who was then carried to the church’s graveyard on the opposite side of the harbor. Every tiny, lovingly made garment was packed away by Miss Winifred and Thirza, along with the ruffled basket that had been decorated with frills and lace to hold downy-headed, dimpled limbs. There little Joy would never rest, having obtained a narrower, colder bed instead.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0024 }

“This has proved a terrible letdown for me,” Miss Winifred uttered with a sigh. “I’ve anticipated this child—and I really wished it would be a girl, as well.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0025 }

“I can only be glad that Nell did not die,” Thirza said, trembling as she remembered those dark hours when the girl she held dear was hovering on the brink of death.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0026 }

“Her heart is broken, poor, poor lamb!” said Tabitha.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0027 }

“I ENVY Nell,” Lorna uttered with sudden fierceness, “and even if she had died, I’d still envy her! For one beautiful day, she was a mother. For THAT, I’d give my life gladly!”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0028 }

“Lorna, my dear, I would avoid speaking in that manner,” Miss Winifred remarked with disapproval. She worried that Miss Abernethy, in her dignity, would view Lorna as utterly dreadful.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0029 }

The recovery of Nell took a considerable length of time, rendered painful to her owing to numerous causes. She was deeply irritated by the brightness and warmth of the Seven Gulls realm; nevertheless, during periods of heavy rainfall, her mind conjured images of the water striking relentlessly against that tiny burial plot on the far side of the harbor; and whenever gusts swept about the rooflines, she detected mournful tones within them that she had not previously perceived.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0030 }

Sympathetic visitors also caused her pain through the good-intentioned cliches they used in an attempt to cloak the starkness of loss. A note sent by Cressy Hale served as another painful blow. Having received news about the child being born, but being unaware that it had died, Cressy sent Nell a letter filled with joyous congratulations that caused her immense suffering.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0031 }

“Had my infant been with me, I could have shared a joyous laugh about it,” she wept to Thirza. “Yet lacking my child, it feels like nothing short of mindless malice—even as I recognize that Cressy would never willingly cause me pain. Oh, Thirza, I fail to understand how I can EVER regain happiness—EVERY single thing will cause me sorrow for as long as I live.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0032 }

“You will be aided by time,” stated Thirza, who was torn apart by compassion yet lacked the ability to convey it except through time-honored clichés.
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0033 }

“It does not appear JUST,” Nell stated in defiance. “Infants come into the world and exist in places where they are unwelcome—where they face neglect—where they are denied any opportunity. I would have adored my child immensely—and nurtured it with such gentleness—and striven to afford her all possibilities for a righteous life. Even so, I was forbidden from retaining her.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0034 }

“It was the Lord’s desire, Nell,” Thirza uttered, powerless when facing the mystery of existence—the reason behind unearned suffering. “And young Joy is in a finer place.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0035 }

“I can’t believe THAT,” Nell exclaimed with bitterness. Upon observing Thirza’s shocked expression, she continued with passion, “Why ought she to be brought into the world—why ought any person to be brought into the world—if her death makes her better off? I DON’T hold the belief that dying at birth is preferable for a baby over living out its full existence—and loving as well as being loved—and experiencing joy alongside suffering—and completing its duties—and forming a character that endows it with an eternal personality. Furthermore, what makes you certain it aligned with God’s will? It might have simply been an obstruction of His design caused by the Power of Evil. One cannot expect us to accept THAT with resignation.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0036 }

“Oh, Nell, do not speak in that manner,” Thirza stated, truly frightened that Nell might be wading into perilous and profound depths. “Understanding is beyond us—yet our faith must remain intact—it is ESSENTIAL to believe that everything happens for the best. I realize it is difficult for you to hold that view at present. Nevertheless, strive to show courage—on account of Hugh. Your condition causes him great anxiety. Your recovery of strength is not progressing as rapidly as it ought to.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0037 }

“Oh, I am aware of how extremely self-centered I have been,” Nell uttered with a sigh. “My affection for Hugh is stronger than it has ever been—and I desire to go on living because of him. Yet I feel as though a portion of my being remains interred in that small cemetery by the harbor—and the pain is so intense that I am terrified of existing.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0038 }

“Always, the pain will not be this intense, Nell.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0039 }

“The idea that the pain might cease at times causes me greater distress than anything else, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0040 }

“Indeed, I am aware of that, as I have experienced the same feeling regarding different matters. Nevertheless, every one of us holds you dear, Nell. Daily visits have been made by Captain Saul to inquire after your condition—while Mrs. Vane constantly frequents the area—and the majority of her hours, it seems to me, are spent by Miss Tolley preparing delicious food for you. This is not particularly to Tabitha’s liking. Her belief is that her own culinary skills equal those of Miss Tolley.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0041 }

“Dearest Tabitha! Oh, Thirza, everyone has shown such fondness and goodness and beauty toward me. I am not without gratitude—and maybe—once this dreadful pain subsides even slightly—I will discover that I am able to continue my life.”
{: #nw-v04-c19-p0042 }
